Write the commit message for the changes below. Reply with the message only: no explanation, no quotes, no markdown fences.

Format: Conventional Commits.
- First line: `type(scope): subject`. The scope is optional: leave it out when it adds nothing.
- Types: feat (new behaviour), fix (a bug), refactor, perf, docs, test, build, ci, style, chore.
- Subject: English, imperative mood ("add", not "added"), lower case after the colon, at most 72 characters, no full stop.
- Always follow the subject with a blank line and a detailed body of bullet points starting with "- ".
- Cover every meaningful group of changes: features, affected modules, schema/validation/seed updates, version bumps, bug fixes and test changes when present. Group related changes; never list the files mechanically.
- Explain what changed and why it matters. Include concrete technical details that help a reviewer understand the change, such as module or service names, old/new versions, rule counts, and the cause of a bug when the diff establishes it.
- Use as many bullet points as needed for complete coverage; do not cap the body at 3 lines or shorten it to fit the subject limit. The 72-character limit applies only to the subject.
- Base every claim on the supplied changes. Do not invent reasons, versions, counts, test results, or details of omitted or truncated content.
- One commit, one type: choose the type of the main change.
- No emoji, no ticket numbers you were not given.

Subjects of the latest commits of this project (follow their scopes and wording, but always include the detailed body required above):
- Show the app as VIce Bartender: product name, window and menu titles, permission text, README
- README: credit the macOS 27 work and describe how ordering works on 27
- Merge macOS 27 support from jordanbaird/Ice#995 (RabenkoYevhenii) and rename its XPC service
- Rename to VIce Bartender: new bundle identifier, own update feed, fork notice
- Conceal again when the launch window runs out
- Do not photograph Ice's own item after all
- Offer to restart the menu bar when macOS stops drawing an item
- Never conceal an application whose item has not appeared

+---
+title: "VIce Bartender: icon and camera gap on macOS 27.2 come from assessment mode"
+author: Vinhnt
+date: 2026-11-11
+branch: macos-27
+cost: { minutes: 1, tokens: 1424 }
+touches:
+  - Ice.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj

+  - Ice/MenuBar/MacOS27/NativeAllowListConcealer27.swift
+  - Ice/Permissions/AppPermissions.swift
+  - Ice/Permissions/Permission.swift
+  - Ice/Permissions/PermissionsView.swift
+---
+
+## Decided
+- Root cause of the missing menu bar icon: on macOS 27.2 the app cannot read group.com.apple.controlcenter (cfprefsd logs 'requires user-preference-read or file-read-data sandbox access'; TCC kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAppDataDetailed 'would require user interaction'). NativeAllowListConcealer27.isAvailable is false, so Concealer27 falls back to assessment mode, where MenuBarAgent drops items of locally signed apps (VIce's own icon, VOpenKey AI) but their processes still report frames through AX.
+- The camera indicator gap: CaptureIndicator27 sits left of MenuBarItemProvider27.leftEdge, which counted the dropped apps' phantom frames. Fix: ItemDrawing27.isListed keeps only items the MenuBarAgent bar window lists (probe: AXWindows of com.apple.MenuBarAgent, children frames).
+- Added ControlCenterPermission (shown with status dots in the Permissions window and Advanced settings) and Concealer27.requestNativeAccess, which opens the plist directly so macOS can ask, retried on app activation.
+## Tried and ruled out
+- A direct open at launch while the screen is locked returns false at once and shows no prompt, so launch alone is not enough.
+## Watch out
+- Never verified that the prompt appears and that native mode brings the icon back: the screen was locked during the session. Check with: log show --predicate 'subsystem == "vn.io.lssoft.vicebartender" AND category == "Concealer27"' and the AX probe of VIce's own AXExtrasMenuBar (Ice.ControlItem.Visible must be on the built-in display).

+//
+//  PermissionStatusBadge.swift
+//  Ice

+
+import SwiftUI
+
+// MARK: - PermissionStatus
+
+/// Where a permission stands, in the terms the interface shows it.
+enum PermissionStatus: Equatable {
+    /// The app has the permission.
+    case granted
+    /// The app does not have the permission, and cannot work properly without it.
+    case missingRequired
+    /// The app does not have the permission, and can work in a limited mode without it.
+    case missingOptional
+
+    /// The colour of the status dot: green for granted, red for what the app cannot do
+    /// without, orange for what it can.
+    var color: Color {
+        switch self {
+        case .granted: .green
+        case .missingRequired: .red
+        case .missingOptional: .orange
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The text beside the dot. The colour is never the only thing that tells the states apart.
+    var label: LocalizedStringKey {
+        switch self {
+        case .granted: "Granted"
+        case .missingRequired, .missingOptional: "Not Granted"
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// What VoiceOver says, which also tells whether the missing permission matters.
+    var accessibilityLabel: LocalizedStringKey {
+        switch self {
+        case .granted: "Granted"
+        case .missingRequired: "Not granted, required"
+        case .missingOptional: "Not granted, optional"
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+// MARK: - PermissionStatusBadge
+
+/// A coloured dot with the status of a permission beside it, the way System Settings shows
+/// the state of a service.
+struct PermissionStatusBadge: View {
+    let status: PermissionStatus
+
+    var body: some View {
+        HStack(spacing: 6) {
+            Circle()
+                .fill(status.color)
+                .frame(width: 8, height: 8)
+                // A hairline keeps the dot defined on the light card, where green and orange are pale.
+                .overlay(Circle().strokeBorder(.black.opacity(0.15), lineWidth: 0.5))
+            Text(status.label)
+                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
+                .contentTransition(.opacity)
+        }
+        .font(.callout)
+        .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.2), value: status)
+        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
+        .accessibilityLabel(Text(status.accessibilityLabel))
+    }
+}

+#!/bin/bash
+# Shared by version.sh, test.sh, dev.sh and release.sh. Source it, do not run it.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+PROJECT="$ROOT/Ice.xcodeproj"
+SCHEME="Ice"
+DISPLAY_NAME="VIce Bartender"          # what the user reads, also the name of the app bundle: VIce Bartender.app
+BUNDLE_ID="vn.io.lssoft.vicebartender" # the app target; its helper is $BUNDLE_ID.MenuBarItemService and is versioned on its own
+
+say()  { printf '\033[1m==> %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; } # stderr: stdout is for values a function returns
+warn() { printf '\033[33mwarning:\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
+die()  { printf '\033[31merror:\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+APP_NAME="VIceBartender"  # the part of the release FILE names (no spaces): VIceBartender-<version>.dmg. Never use it where a person reads the name.
+
+# The certificate used to sign: SIGN_IDENTITY if set, otherwise the first "Developer ID Application" in the keychain.
+find_identity() {
+    if [ -n "${SIGN_IDENTITY:-}" ]; then echo "$SIGN_IDENTITY"; return; fi
+    security find-identity -v -p codesigning | sed -n 's/.*"\(Developer ID Application:[^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
+}
+
+# "Developer ID Application: Name (TEAMID)" -> TEAMID
+team_of() { echo "$1" | sed -n 's/.*(\([A-Z0-9]*\))$/\1/p'; }
+
+# build <Debug|Release> <derived data dir> <extra xcodebuild args...>  ->  prints the path of the built app
+# The project is set up for automatic signing with the original author's team, so signing is overridden here: the same Developer ID
+# certificate every time, which also keeps the permissions you granted (Accessibility, Screen Recording) from one build to the next.
+build_app() {
+    local configuration="$1" derived="$2"; shift 2
+    local identity; identity="$(find_identity)"
+    [ -n "$identity" ] || die "no 'Developer ID Application' certificate in the keychain (set SIGN_IDENTITY to use another)"
+    local team; team="$(team_of "$identity")"
+    say "Building $DISPLAY_NAME ($configuration), signed as: $identity"
+    xcodebuild -project "$PROJECT" -scheme "$SCHEME" -configuration "$configuration" -derivedDataPath "$derived" \
+        CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="$identity" DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$team" PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER="" \
+        "$@" build > "$derived.log" 2>&1 || { grep -E 'error:' "$derived.log" | head -20 >&2; die "build failed, full log: $derived.log"; }
+    echo "$derived/Build/Products/$configuration/$DISPLAY_NAME.app"
+}
